code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Standard physics (Chapman 1919 + Yamazaki & Maute 2017 Sq currents + Kim & Chang 2018 ensemble) explains eclipse-day magnetic perturbations as ionospheric conductivity response. The dome FSF is a geometric ratio with no standard counterpart — a relabel critique would require an equivalent standard quantity to be re-named. Standard physics also predicts station-to-station variation by geomagnetic latitude, which incidentally tracks geographic latitude; that is a causal-confound critique (carried by WIN-025/068), not a relabel.

code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: Structurally yes: FSF = (H(r)/r)/(H(r_BOU)/r_BOU) with H(r) = 8537 × exp(−r/8619) under V12 ellipse. A derivation path from dome parameters to per-station ratios exists in principle. BUT the V51 station radii r_k are themselves back-derived from r·tan(theta_Polaris) = H(r), so under V51 the entire ratio collapses to tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) (verified by independent computation in quantitative_verification below; identity RMSE 0.0061 vs locked-formula 0.0121 across 9 stations). The surviving dome content under V51 is therefore the assignment of "Boulder = 40.015°N reference latitude" — and the c8 verification + this c9 verification both confirm 40.015 is the city-centroid lat (the INTERMAGNET BOU observatory is at 40.137°N which gives identity-RMSE 0.0094, much worse). Whatever V12 content the formula started with cancels under the V51 coordinate normalization.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome author did several things genuinely better than the typical WIN here. He registered nine station-specific, falsifiable numerical predictions (raw-text/03-predictions.txt:26-34) with explicit coverage factors and ±tolerance bands ahead of a dated natural experiment (2026-08-12 eclipse, raw-text/03-predictions.txt:18), then attempted to compress them into a closed-form scaling law with a stated goodness-of-fit (the LOCKED 2026-03-22 FSF(lat) paragraph cited verbatim in EXP-617). That is real epistemic exposure (wins.json WIN-044.detail_evidence: "Registered 2026-03-12 | Git + OpenTimestamps anchored"). The underlying intuition — eclipse-day ΔZ varies systematically by station latitude — is empirically respectable (cf. WIN-068 finding citing Kim & Chang 2018 ensemble). Publishing a per-station residual table and explicit ±error bars is more transparency than most WINs offer, and monitor.py Domain 10 honestly marks the eclipse PENDING rather than backfilling a confirmation (per c7 dome_code_analysis assessment).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Exposure is not derivation. (1) The registered FSF table reproduces tan(lat)/tan(40.015°) to published precision at the core stations (independent computation this run: HAD identity −0.0004, CLF identity −0.0010, NGK identity −0.0005, ESK identity −0.0007, LER identity −0.0008 — all within ≤0.0012 of published, code_analysis.derives_from_dome_evidence verifies). Under the V51 Polaris-equation r_k assignment the published FSF table contains essentially zero dome information beyond a latitude choice for the BOU reference (data/wins.json WIN-044.detail_evidence). (2) The LOCKED 2026-03-22 replacement formula has three free constants (0.19550, 0.1640, 32.974) with no derivation path from any dome parameter, its RMSE annotation is fit-language not derivation, and on independent recomputation the identity beats it at 7 of 9 stations including HAD (data/wins.json WIN-044.detail_evidence; cross-referenced to Section 4.2.4 via #p4-424). (3) Prospective registration tests the prediction in August 2026 but cannot confirm anything before that window opens — and the structural finding that the formula is essentially globe trigonometry is invariant to the eclipse-day measurement outcome (data/wins.json WIN-044.code_analysis.derives_from_dome_evidence).

advocate_mode.best_defense: The tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) collapse is not a refutation of V12 dome physics — it is the dome\u2019s observable signature, derived correctly. Under V51, station radii r_k are back-computed from r·tan(theta_Polaris_star) = H(r), where theta_Polaris depends on n(r), the dome\u2019s aetheric refraction medium. The n(r) profile is fitted to make the sun-altitude observation work (Section 1.8), so n(r) IS dome physics. The chain n(r) -> theta_Polaris(lat) -> r_k -> FSF(r_k) carries dome content end-to-end, even if the algebraic form of FSF as a function of latitude happens to coincide with a tangent ratio. You\u2019ve only shown that the dome\u2019s predicted observable looks like globe trigonometry — you have NOT shown that the derivation contains no dome content. The same critique could apply to General Relativity: light deflection under GR matches a Newtonian-doubled approximation in the weak-field limit, but no one says GR therefore "reduces to Newton with a factor of 2 and contains zero relativistic content." Form-coincidence in the observable is not equivalent to absence of derivation. Furthermore, the version-instability claim (1.47 V51 vs 1.89 V50.6) is normal scientific refinement: early GR\u2019s metric forms changed too, and that did not falsify the framework. The 28% HAD swing across V50.6 → V51 reflects the dome author\u2019s honest refinement of n(r), not a parameter-fit. The locked-formula RMSE is goodness-of-fit reporting, which is what derivations of empirical observables routinely include (e.g., quantum electrodynamics anomalous magnetic moment).
